newsitem.title: UK: Sterling climbs to 53-month high vs mark in Europe.
newsitem.headline: Sterling climbs to 53-month high vs mark in Europe.

text.p: Sterling continued to rise against the mark through most of the European session to touch a 53-month high of 2.7688 marks, drawing strength from the dollar's rally against the German currency.
It backed off its high to stand at 2.7615/25 at 1622 GMT, but this was still more than two pfennigs above its late Monday European level of 2.7437/44.

"The main feature as far as sterling's rise (against the mark) today is concerned is direction from dollar/mark. And although it seems to have halted a bit, I think it can go further," said a trader at a U.S. bank in London.
Cable, meanwhile, was at $1.6137/45 against late Monday's $1.6188/98, struggling in the face of the dollar's latest show of strength.

The dollar earlier rose to a fresh 34-month high of 1.7137 marks, boosted by comments by Federal Reserve chairman Alan Greenspan that it was crucial to keep inflation down, and also by robust U.S. home sales data.
Traders said cable appeared to be having a hard time breaking convincingly back above $1.6170 after dropping through this chart level overnight.
